name: Rangamati
tagline: The blue lake among the hills — Kaptai's waters, the hanging bridge, and the living cultures of the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

guide.bestTime: October to March (cool, dry, clear lake views). The hill new-year Boisabi falls in mid-April; Kathin Chibar Dan at Rajban Vihara is in late autumn.
guide.gettingThere: By road from Chattogram (~75 km, ~2.5 hr) or Dhaka (~310 km, ~8–9 hr by overnight coach). Within the district the boat is king — Kaptai Lake is the highway, and most sights are reached by engine-boat. The Chittagong Hill Tracts is a sensitive border region: check current travel advisories, and note that some upazilas (and travel for foreign nationals) may require prior permission.
guide.difficulty: Moderate — the town and lake are easy, but hill destinations like Sajek and Shuvolong mean long boat or jeep journeys. Respect local communities, and check the security and permission situation before heading into remote upazilas.

mustVisit.name: Kaptai Lake
mustVisit.description: The largest man-made lake in Bangladesh — a vast sheet of blue water threading between forested hills, dotted with islands and the everyday boats of the people who live along it.
mustVisit.history: The lake was formed in the early 1960s when the Kaptai Dam was built across the Karnaphuli river for hydroelectric power. The reservoir flooded a huge area — including the old Chakma royal capital and much prime farmland — and reshaped life across the hill tracts.

practical.hours: Best by day; boats from Rangamati town ghats

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: The lake wraps around Rangamati town itself
howToReach.transport: Engine-boat or country boat from the town ghats

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool, dry months for the clearest blue water
tips: Hire a boat for a half-day to reach Shuvolong and the island restaurants
Agree the boat fare and route before setting off
Carry water and sun protection — there is little shade on the water

mustVisit.name: Rangamati Hanging Bridge
mustVisit.description: The 335-foot suspension footbridge over an arm of Kaptai Lake — the picture-postcard symbol of Rangamati, swaying gently above the blue water.
mustVisit.history: Built by the tourism authority as the district's signature attraction, the colourful 'jhulonto bridge' links two hills across an inlet of the lake. It occasionally closes when high water submerges the deck.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: At the Parjatan complex, Rangamati Sadar

mustVisit.bestTime: Morning or late afternoon for the light on the lake
tips: Check before visiting in the monsoon — it can be underwater
It gets crowded on holidays; go early

mustVisit.name: Sajek Valley
mustVisit.description: The 'queen of hills' — a high ridge of rolling green and cloud in Baghaichhari, where the sunrise breaks over a sea of mist and the nights are cold and starry.
mustVisit.history: Sajek lies in the far north of Rangamati district, home to Lushai, Pankho and Tripura communities. It has become one of the country's most popular hill getaways, with cottages strung along the ridge.

practical.hours: Overnight stays; vehicles travel in scheduled convoys

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: In Baghaichhari, far north Rangamati — usually reached via Khagrachhari (Dighinala), not from Rangamati town
howToReach.transport: Jeep ('chander gari') from Khagrachhari, often in an army-escorted convoy

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool months for clear sunrises; the cloud is thickest after rain
tips: Book a cottage ahead — Sajek fills up on weekends and holidays
Travel times follow the convoy schedule; plan around it
Carry cash and check the current security situation before going

mustVisit.name: Shuvolong Waterfall
mustVisit.description: A waterfall tumbling down a hillside straight toward Kaptai Lake in Barkal — reached only by boat, the cascade fullest after the rains.
mustVisit.history: Shuvolong (Subhalong) is one of several falls in the area, and the most visited because a boat can pull right up to its foot. Around it rise steep hills and quiet hill-community villages.

practical.hours: Daylight; go by boat from Rangamati

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: In Barkal, reached by engine-boat across Kaptai Lake (~1–1.5 hr)

mustVisit.bestTime: Just after the monsoon, when the fall is at full flow
tips: The fall shrinks in the dry season — temper expectations in winter
Combine with a longer Kaptai Lake boat tour

mustVisit.name: Rajban Vihara
mustVisit.description: The largest Buddhist monastery in Bangladesh — a serene 33-acre complex on the edge of Kaptai Lake, founded under the revered meditation master Bana Bhante.
mustVisit.history: Established in the 1970s at the initiative of the Chakma royal family, Rajban Vihara became the seat of Sadhanananda Mahasthabir (Bana Bhante). Its annual Kathin Chibar Dan — in which robes are woven and offered to monks within 24 hours — draws pilgrims from across the hill tracts and beyond.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: On the lakeshore in Rangamati Sadar

mustVisit.bestTime: Kathin Chibar Dan (late autumn) for the festival; mornings for quiet
tips: Dress modestly and remove shoes in the shrine
Maintain silence — it is an active meditation monastery

mustVisit.name: Chakma Rajbari
mustVisit.description: The palace of the Chakma Circle Chief — the seat of one of the three traditional 'circle' kingdoms of the Chittagong Hill Tracts, and a window into Chakma royal heritage.
mustVisit.history: The present Chakma Rajbari was built in 1960 at the new Rangamati town, after the old royal capital was lost beneath Kaptai Lake. The Chakma Raja remains the customary head of the Chakma Circle. The nearby Tribal Cultural Institute Museum displays the dress, tools and crafts of the hill peoples.

practical.hours: Exterior viewable by day; the museum keeps its own hours

mustVisit.bestTime: Daytime; pair with the Tribal Cultural Institute Museum
tips: It is a private residence — view respectfully from outside
The museum nearby is the better place to learn the hill cultures

specialties.name: Bamboo Chicken (Sumoh Huro)
specialties.description: The Chakma signature — chicken stuffed with herbs into a green bamboo tube and cooked over fire, taking its aroma from the bamboo itself. Any dish cooked this way is a 'sumoh gorang'.
specialties.venue: Rangamati hill-cuisine restaurants and island eateries

specialties.name: Backstrap-Loom Weaving (Pinon-Hadi)
specialties.description: Chakma and Marma women weave bright, intricately patterned cloth on backstrap looms — the pinon-hadi (the women's traditional wrap and shawl) is the best-known piece.
specialties.venue: Rangamati weaving markets and the Tribal Cultural Institute

specialties.name: Boisabi
specialties.description: The shared hill new-year festival — Chakma Biju, Marma Sangrai and Tripura Boisuk together — with flower offerings, the pajon feast, water-throwing and dance in mid-April.

specialties.name: Kathin Chibar Dan
specialties.description: A Buddhist robe-offering festival at Rajban Vihara in which a robe is spun, woven and offered to the monks within 24 hours — drawing huge crowds of devotees in late autumn.

bucketlist.title: Cross the Rangamati Hanging Bridge
bucketlist.detail: Walk the swaying 335-foot suspension bridge over an arm of Kaptai Lake — the district's signature view.

bucketlist.title: Take an engine-boat across Kaptai Lake
bucketlist.detail: On the largest man-made lake in the country, the boat is the road — glide between forested islands and hill villages.

bucketlist.title: Watch sunrise over the clouds at Sajek
bucketlist.detail: The 'queen of hills' floats above a sea of mist at dawn — cold nights, starry skies and rolling green by day.

bucketlist.title: Boat to Shuvolong Waterfall
bucketlist.detail: A waterfall that pours toward the lake in Barkal, reached only by boat and fullest after the rains.

bucketlist.title: Find quiet at Rajban Vihara
bucketlist.detail: The largest Buddhist monastery in Bangladesh, founded under the revered Bana Bhante, on the edge of the lake.

bucketlist.title: Witness Kathin Chibar Dan
bucketlist.detail: A robe spun, woven and offered to the monks within 24 hours — a Buddhist festival that fills Rajban Vihara each late autumn.

bucketlist.title: Eat bamboo chicken
bucketlist.detail: Chicken cooked inside a green bamboo tube with hill herbs — the Chakma 'sumoh huro', smoky and fragrant.

bucketlist.title: Try hebang and pajon
bucketlist.detail: Bamboo-tube dishes (hebang) and the mixed-vegetable pajon — herb-forward, low on spice, full of the hills.

bucketlist.title: Visit the Tribal Cultural Institute Museum
bucketlist.detail: The dress, tools, instruments and crafts of the Chakma, Marma, Tanchangya, Tripura and other hill peoples under one roof.

bucketlist.title: Buy a handwoven pinon-hadi
bucketlist.detail: Bright backstrap-loom cloth woven by Chakma and Marma women — buy it from the weavers themselves.

bucketlist.title: Join the Boisabi hill new year
bucketlist.detail: Flowers floated on the water, the pajon feast, water-throwing and dance as Chakma, Marma and Tripura see in the new year together.

bucketlist.title: Eat at a floating lake restaurant
bucketlist.detail: Island eateries like Peda Ting Ting serve Chakma food with the lake lapping at the deck.

foods.name: Bamboo Chicken (Sumoh Huro)
foods.description: Chicken and herbs cooked inside a green bamboo tube over fire — the Chakma signature dish.

foods.name: Hebang
foods.description: Fish or vegetables wrapped and steamed in banana leaf inside bamboo — a fragrant, near spice-free hill preparation.

foods.name: Pajon (Pachon)
foods.description: A medley of many seasonal vegetables and hillside herbs cooked together — the festive dish of Biju/Boisabi.

foods.name: Nappi-flavoured Dishes
foods.description: Hill cooking often built on nappi (fermented fish/shrimp paste) for a deep, pungent base.

foods.name: Binni Rice
foods.description: Sticky 'binni' rice, sometimes cooked in bamboo, eaten plain or with hill sweets.

foods.name: Kaptai Lake Fish
foods.description: Freshwater fish from the lake — kechki, chapila and more — fried fresh or in light curries.

famousPeople.name: Sadhanananda Mahasthabir (Bana Bhante)
famousPeople.knownFor: Revered Theravada Buddhist meditation master and founding spiritual head of Rajban Vihara; born Rathindra Chakma at Moghban in Rangamati Sadar. One of the most venerated monks of the hill tracts.

didYouKnow: Rangamati is the largest district in Bangladesh by area (6,116 sq km), and the majority of its people are indigenous — Chakma, Marma, Tanchangya, Tripura and others.
Kaptai Lake, the largest man-made lake in the country, was formed in the early 1960s by the Kaptai Dam on the Karnaphuli — the rising water submerged the old Chakma royal capital and much farmland.
The Rangamati Hanging Bridge, a 335-foot suspension footbridge over an arm of the lake, is the district's best-known symbol.
Rajban Vihara, founded in the 1970s under the revered monk Bana Bhante, is the largest Buddhist monastery in Bangladesh; its Kathin Chibar Dan festival sees a robe woven and offered within 24 hours.
Sajek Valley, the 'queen of hills', lies within Rangamati's Baghaichhari upazila though it is usually reached through neighbouring Khagrachhari.
